answer: Proof-of-stake mechanisms utilize staked capital as a barrier to entry, functioning like a structural jetty that prevents the uncontrolled expansion of fake identities. By requiring agents to lock assets within a cryptographically verifiable shale of data, the system imposes a fiscal cost proportional to the desired influence. Like a harsh tundra environment, this scarcity ensures that malicious actors face prohibitive costs, effectively isolating Sybil nodes from gaining control over the consensus protocol.
